title: Deploy a Spring Boot application on managed hosting
summary: Match the Java runtime, assigned port, external configuration, storage and release checks to the host.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Deploy Spring Boot App on Heroku: Easy Guide for Beginners

richText: Managed hosting provides an environment in which your application process runs. You still choose the artifact, runtime settings, database access and application checks.
Build the executable JAR with the project’s wrapper and declared Java version. Select a host runtime that supports that Java version.
Bind to the port assigned by the platform. In the Heroku example, PORT is supplied at runtime and Spring can read it through a property placeholder.
Keep database connections and external API credentials in the host’s configuration or secret system. Keep application defaults in the artifact.
A Procfile tells the classic Heroku process model how to launch a web process. The JAR path must match the artifact your build actually produces.

# application.properties
server.port=${PORT:8080}

# Procfile, with Maven finalName set to journal
web: java -jar target/journal.jar
An application restart must not lose user data. Use an external database and persistent object storage when needed; do not depend on an ephemeral application filesystem.
For MongoDB Atlas, configure the database user and the network access rules needed by the host. A URI alone does not grant network access.
Read the platform build log, process log and application startup log separately. A successful upload does not prove the process started.
Confirm the app binds to the required port and answers a readiness request. Then check a representative authenticated API request and a database read/write.
Platform termination and restart are normal possibilities. Handle shutdown and make retried operations safe rather than assuming a process runs forever.
The playlist’s Heroku lesson is a deployment topic. Follow the current instructions for the Heroku generation and runtime you use rather than treating old commands as a fixed contract.
Record which application revision and configuration were released. Diagnose a failing revision using its logs, not the last successful local build.
Keep the prior artifact available for rollback. A code rollback does not automatically reverse a database migration or restore deleted data.
Use managed hosting when its supported runtime and operations model fit the application. Use a VPS when you need control of the machine and can maintain it.
